role: How users prove who they are

options.label: Server session cookies
options.notes: Easiest mental model; revocation is trivial; needs sticky/shared session store at scale.

reasons.simplicity: One server-side record; revoke by deleting it.
reasons.scalability: Needs a shared/sticky session store across instances.
reasons.security: Server-controlled; easy revocation; CSRF must be handled.

options.label: Stateless JWT
options.notes: Scales horizontally with no session store; revocation and token theft are the hard parts.

reasons.simplicity: Token carries claims; no session store, but revocation logic is extra work.
reasons.scalability: No shared state — scales horizontally cleanly.
reasons.security: Can't revoke a leaked token without a denylist; keep TTL short.

contraindications: apps needing instant revocation without a denylist

options.label: Delegated OAuth / social login
options.notes: No passwords to hold; depends on third-party IdP; still need local account linking.

reasons.simplicity: No password storage, but IdP integration + account linking add steps.
reasons.scalability: Offloads auth load to the IdP.
reasons.security: No passwords to leak; depends on IdP security and correct token validation.

options.label: Managed auth (Clerk/Auth0-style)
options.notes: Fastest to ship and offloads security; recurring cost and vendor lock-in; outside the yard.

reasons.security: Vendor hardened, but data leaves your boundary and you inherit their incidents.
